title: Bharata's journey
hook: the son a mother schemed for turns on her, and then has to convince another mother he never wanted any of it

segments.voice: Yesterday: Bharata's journey, part one. He came home to a silent city, and Kaikeyi told him, as if it were good news, that the throne was his. Did you read a room before you spoke? Today the week closes. Day five hundred forty-six.

Kaikeyi has been waiting for this conversation. Her son home, the crown ready. And what she gets is fury. Bharata doesn't thank her. He tells her she has destroyed the family, killed his father with grief, and sent away the brother he loves. He says the kingdom she won for him is something he will never accept. And then he walks out, to face the person he dreads most: Kausalya, Rama's mother.
screen: `NO THANKS, ONLY GRIEF.` → `I WILL NEVER ACCEPT IT.` → `NOW, KAUSALYA.`

segments.voice: Kausalya has every reason to suspect him. Here is the son who gains everything from her son's exile. She tells him so, bitterly: you wanted the kingdom, now you have it. Take me to Rama too. Bharata falls at her feet. And then he swears. Valmiki gives him a long chain of oaths, each one naming a wrong he'd rather be guilty of than this. May I carry the guilt of someone who betrays a trust, who strikes a sleeping person, who turns away a guest, if I ever wanted Rama gone. It goes on and on, a son emptying himself out. Kausalya believes him. She takes his head in her lap and they weep together. Then the duty that couldn't wait. Under Vasishtha's guidance, Bharata performs his father's funeral rites. The body is taken from the oil, the fire is lit, the queens and the city mourn, and the family offers water at the Sarayu. Afterward, at the palace, Shatrughna catches Manthara, the maid who started it all, and starts to drag her. Bharata stops him. Rama, he says, would never forgive us. Now the week. On Chitrakoot, a hut and a green hill, a sort of peace. In Ayodhya, a king's confession: a sound in the dark, a water pot, a father's curse. A death past midnight. A boy with no name who became Shravan Kumar. And this son, called home without being told, who refuses the prize his mother won for him.
screen: `KAUSALYA'S SUSPICION.` · `A CHAIN OF OATHS.` · `THE KING'S LAST RITES.` · `THE WEEK, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `HE REFUSES THE PRIZE.`

segments.voice: Sit and let your shoulders drop. Think of a time someone suspected you of something you didn't do, or a time you suspected someone who turned out to be innocent. Don't argue it again. Just notice where it sits in your body: the jaw, the chest, the stomach. Breathe into that spot. On each out breath, let it loosen a little, the way Kausalya's suspicion loosened when she finally heard him. The bell holds the time.
Bharata's journey. He rejects his mother's gift, swears his innocence to Kausalya, and performs his father's last rites.
Your line: he refuses the prize. Today, if you notice yourself suspecting someone, ask them one honest question before you decide. Day five hundred forty-six.

screen: `DAY 546 COUNTS.` → `A WEEK OF LOSS AND RETURN, DONE.` → `TOMORROW: BHARATA'S JOURNEY, PART THREE.`

howItsDone: Bharata is honored in Ramayana tradition as a model of loyalty and renunciation; his oaths before Kausalya run on for many verses of the Ayodhya Kanda.

original.note: Sanskrit śapatha: an oath. Bharata swears oath after oath to Kausalya.

trapdoor: what you thought: Bharata is the one who benefits, so he must be part of the plan.
what it means: he rejects the crown and proves his innocence to Rama's mother.
what a scholar hears: Ayodhya 75 is a long list of oaths, each naming a wrong Bharata would rather carry than have wished Rama exiled.

Review (538–556 pass): Kaikeyi did not wait 'years' (Manthara persuaded her on the eve of the coronation), fixed; cut the superlative 'angriest speech in the second book'; the Manthara episode happens at the palace after the rites, not 'on the way' (Ayodhya 78), fixed; the Sarayu is now where water is offered, not where the body is carried (confirm the cremation site in Ayodhya 76); softened 'fills a whole sarga' and 'across Hindu traditions'.
